title: Screen readers: testing properly, not just passing the tool

videos.script: A screen reader does not look at the page. It asks the browser what is there. {{ask}} The browser answers from a tree. Every element has a role, a name, and a state. Button, Book. Textbox, Your name. {{tree}} On the first booking page, the logo has no name. The name field has no name. And Book is not a button at all. It is a word. {{before}} Press Book with the field empty, and the border turns red. The tree does not change. So the screen reader has nothing to say. {{silent}} In this lesson you read that tree from a script, before and after the fixes. {{script}} You give the error a live region, so that it is announced the moment it appears. {{alert}} And you meet the readers themselves. NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, Orca, TalkBack. They run on your own computer, not in the lab, so nothing here pretends to be their speech. {{readers}} What a script can do is write the plan for the session: what to listen for, and which tasks to finish. {{charter}} Then you turn the screen away, and listen. {{listen}}
